title: Ionic and Covalent Compounds
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Ionic and Covalent Compounds Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Elements combine to form compounds: ionic and covalent compounds, naming compounds, and writing chemical formulas. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 9, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 science worksheets (BC): ionic and covalent bonds, naming compounds, writing chemical formulas, and properties of compounds. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Ionic: metal + non-metal. Covalent: non-metals share electrons.
key_sub: Ion charges must add to zero.
body_html:
How to think about it

In an ionic compound, a metal gives electrons to a non-metal, forming positive and negative ions that attract each other (NaCl). Ionic compounds are usually hard solids with high melting points that conduct electricity when dissolved.

In a covalent (molecular) compound, non-metals share electrons (H2O, CO2). To write an ionic formula, balance the charges: Ca2+ and Cl− make CaCl2. Covalent compounds use prefixes: carbon dioxide, dinitrogen tetroxide.

Example

What is the formula of the compound made of Al3+ and O2−?

The charges must add to zero.

Answer: Al2O3

Example

Is CO2 ionic or covalent?

Carbon and oxygen are both non-metals.

Answer: covalent

Common mistakes

  • Using prefixes for ionic compounds (it is calcium chloride, not calcium dichloride).
  • Forgetting to balance the charges.
  • Thinking covalent compounds conduct electricity.
